12	
13	\# Sprint Overview
14	
15	The team planned to complete 12 issues during Sprint 2 (two medium and one small for 535 students and two medium for 435 students). Two additional sub-issues were closed, as their modifications were implemented in a previous sub-issue or as a consequence of a similar issue. Most subissues covered separate issues, with continuation of Sprint 1’s large parent issues being completed.
16	
17	The team delivered several features across language accessibility, display bugfixes, grid layering, shape masking, gradient color picker, and client-to-client QOL features. Work mainly covered front-end tool usage, but client-to-client features were implemented and back-end was understood thoroughly with discussion on future client-to-client work. Additional work included AI usage documentation, midpoint, and diagrams.
18	
19	All assigned issues have been completed. Two issues were closed and replaced with newer issues due to previous implementation as stated above, and one issue was split into two subissues as integration was more complex than originally expected. Workflow was significantly more efficient in this sprint, likely due to better timings with exams, and midpoints implementation. AI usage of students has gotten more efficient and effective, and team members are seen communicating better with both agents and peers with higher consistency.

67	\#Test Strategy
68	
69	Our team used automated tests alongside individual implementation and review of tests to check new behavior and its functionality against pre-existing code. Test cases made by ai were reviewed line by line to understand implementation, alongside explanation by the agent to understand coverage and importance. Code implemented was reviewed by design flow of variables and location in the files directly to understand what changes occurred and how many files it affected.
70	
71	Testing included:
72	
73	- Unit and component tests for new functionality.
74	- Regression testing for existing editor behavior.
75	- Export tests for gradient and SVG behavior.
76	- Validation of configuration, persistence, and compatibility where applicable.
77	- CI checks for typechecking, linting, formatting, and automated tests.
78	- Individual checks to manually test functionality
79	- Individual review of code by a peer to check for errors missed by author & ai.
80	
81	Bucket size being the only CI check has been removed due to incompatibility with yarn monorepo.

133	\# Risks and Retrospective
134	
135	Communication risks have severely lowered. While assignments are procrastinated, a noticeable uptick in when issues are completed has been noted. Risks related to communication have thankfully been mostly mitigated by this point. Bundle Size check has been dropped due to its incompatibility with the inherent characteristics of the mono-repo. Linting has not been an issue, past a miscommunication with excalidraw-room inclusion, but it was fixed.
136	
137	Issues abandoned were implemented without issue, and most issues have been individual and user error.
138	
139	Possible future risks cover mainly design philosophy in architectural design as our changes become more complex and innovative. The second biggest possible risk is the expanding risk of issues poorly covered by test cases, leading to future branch merges leading to failures of features not tracked by the issue, which could lead to silent bugs. To mitigate this possible risk we should likely focus on utilizing AI and external code-checkers to test coverage of newly implemented code.
140	
141	\# Sprint 3 Plan
142	
143	During Sprint 2, we implemented some of our most longstanding issues with Excalidraw. We also focused on completing a previously started large issues subissues and fully doing an entire other large issue. Besides that we started 2 new subissues focused on image filter editing and the other finally started the back end focus for client to client control on visibility and intractability. Lastly we broke issue 40 into 2 subissues to better handle it and completed 1 of the 2 of them this sprint.
144	
145	The back-end client-to-client has been expanded and understood more. We still need deliberation whether client-based administration is worth implementation or a complete overhaul of the client-to-client connection. Our choice on how to go forward or whether we should scrap administrative features and stick to client-side QOL features will be decided and looked into for Sprint 3\.
146	
147	For sprint 3 we want to continue these 3 large issues which are divided into an extra 9 subissue. As well as starting work on some more large issues since the last of the standalone medium and small issues were handled this sprint. ```text
feat(editor): newcomer default and saved collaborator settings (#83) | CashenCroft | open null | + 20285 - 51 
 Closes #83 (Sub-issue of #14)

**Builds on #82 (merged in #180):** this branch is based on `master` after #180, so the diff contains only #83's commits.

## Why

In a busy or open room, a new collaborator is fully interactive on my screen the moment they join, so their drawings can be selected or moved by accident before I notice them. And every choice I make in the collaborator dropdown (who's hidden, who's locked, layering and its order) is lost on reload, so I have to set the room up again each session.

This PR follows the [Design comment on #83](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/83):

- **New collaborators** setting (**Visible / Locked / Hidden**, default **Locked**), applied the first time this client sees someone;
- newcomers placed **below everyone already in #82's layer order**: directly above "unknown / miscellaneous", or at the very bottom if I've moved it up (Criteria D, [amended](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/83#issuecomment-7028370098));
- the dropdown's settings are **saved locally**: the newcomer default for all rooms, and hidden, locked, the Layering switch and the order per room.

As with the rest of #14, everything stays on my device. Nothing reaches the shared scene, exports, other collaborators or undo history.

It builds on:

- **#116:** the collaborator directory ("seen before" = in the directory) and its per-room storage;
- **#81:** locking (hidden → also locked);
- **#82 (#180):** the layer order. Criteria D replaces #82's Criteria H ("newcomers go to the bottom").

## What changed

- **One pure rule.** `getNewcomerState` (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`) gives the state a first-seen collaborator starts in, built on #81's `addLockedCollaborators`. It never applies to me or to miscellaneous. #82's `getCollaboratorLayerOrder` now places newcomers directly above miscellaneous while it's the bottom row, otherwise at the very bottom; my own new client id goes on top.
- **Applied in one place.** `Collab.updateCollaborator` checks "not in the directory yet" before recording the sighting and merges the result into its existing `updateScene`. `recordSighting` is unchanged.
- **One small persistence module.** `excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorSettings.ts`: one versioned localStorage entry next to #116's directory, sharing its room pruning (20 rooms). Sets are stored as arrays; anything unreadable, unknown or from another version falls back to the defaults. Hiding my own drawings is never saved or restored.
- **Restore and save.** Restored when a room starts and right after each scene reset on join (`resetScene` resets all of appState); saved from the app's `onChange` only when a setting changed. This also stops lock and layering state leaking into the next room.
- **State and UI.** `AppState.newCollaboratorDefault` (never persisted with the scene, exported or synced), a `setNewCollaboratorDefault` action (no history), and a Visible / Locked / Hidden row in the dropdown below Layering, using the existing `RadioGroup`, on desktop and phone.
- **Snapshots:** AppState snapshots gain the new field (133 added lines, nothing else).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **Shared room pruning.** The settings module reuses the directory's `readStoredObject` / `withRecentRooms`, so a change to one affects the other.
- **No migration.** Saved settings from another version are ignored and replaced on the next save.
- **One browser profile = one set of saved settings.** Tabs of the same browser share a room's saved settings (last change wins) and the directory, so a collaborator first seen in one tab isn't new in another.
- **Duplicated test mocks** in `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (socket, encryption, Firebase), as in #81/#82 (`vi.mock` is per file).
- **A typed variable in `updateCollaborator`** works around `updateScene` inferring its keys from the object literal.

**Encountered:**

- **`resetScene` resets all of appState** when joining a room; #116 republishes the directory afterwards, and this PR restores the saved settings the same way.
- **The Collab API lives in a global jotai store** that unmounting doesn't clear. Tests that re-render the app must reset it, or the new app drives the old Collab (fixed in `dba1e248` after it made reload tests flaky).
- **#116's room pruning keeps the older room** when two saves land in the same millisecond.
- **Join order after a reload** comes from the directory, which loads newest-first (accepted in #82).
- **Windows-only test setup bug:** 3 `exportToSvg` snapshots fail locally on Windows (on `master` too); CI is unaffected. On a busy machine, the first test of some files can also time out while the app loads.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |

=== ISSUE 83 ===
 # Issue Description

## Summary

Adds a **default for newcomers** and **saved settings** to the collaborator dropdown from #116, #81 and #82.

- **Newcomer default.** A "New collaborators" setting (**Visible / Locked / Hidden**, default **Locked**) decides how a collaborator is treated the first time this client sees them. With the default, newcomers' drawings are visible but can't be selected or edited (#81's visible-only mode) until I unlock them.
- **Newcomers in the layer order.** While layering is on (#82), a newcomer is placed last, **directly above "unknown / miscellaneous"**.
- **Saved settings.** This menu's settings are remembered locally across page reloads: the newcomer default, hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the Layering switch, and the layer order.

Like the rest of this menu, everything is local to my client. It never changes the shared scene or what other collaborators see.

## User Story

**As a** collaborator in a busy or open room, **I want** people I see for the first time to start visible but locked on my screen, and my visibility, lock and layering choices to be remembered, **so that** newcomers can't be accidentally edited or clutter my view, and I don't have to set everything up again each session.

## User Scenario

A team lead runs a design session in a shared room. Before anyone new arrives, the "New collaborators" setting is already on Locked (the default). When a new student joins and starts drawing, the lead can see the student's work but can't accidentally select or move it. Because layering is on, the student is placed just above Miscellaneous in the layer order. The lead unlocks the student once they've settled in. The next day, the lead reopens the room: the layering order, the hidden and locked collaborators, and the newcomer setting are all as they left them. Nobody else in the room sees any of these settings.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium

**Specific:** Lesser Medium (5 points)

**Reason:** Builds on #116 (collaborator directory, which already records each collaborator the first time they're seen, and is already saved per room), #81 (locking) and #82 (layer order). This issue adds one setting, applies it at the point the directory records a new collaborator, changes where newcomers enter the layer order, and adds a small local persistence layer that saves and restores this menu's settings. It touches no element data, sync, or server code.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Criteria A: Newcomer default setting.** The collaborator dropdown has a "New collaborators" setting with three options: Visible, Locked, Hidden. It defaults to **Locked**.
- [ ] **Criteria B: Applied to first-seen collaborators.** When this client sees a collaborator for the first time (they aren't in the collaborator directory yet), they start in the chosen state: Visible → visible and interactive; Locked → visible but locked; Hidden → hidden (and therefore locked, per #81). A collaborator seen before (in the directory, even if they left) is not affected when they rejoin.
- [ ] **Criteria C: Only future newcomers.** Changing the setting doesn't change any collaborator already seen. The existing Show all / Hide all / Lock all / Unlock all controls still work for them.
- [ ] **Criteria D: Newcomers in the layer order.** While layering is on, a newcomer is added below every collaborator already in the order: directly above "unknown / miscellaneous" while it's the bottom row, or at the very bottom if I've moved it up. Several newcomers are added in join order. This replaces #82's Criteria H ("added to the bottom").
- [ ] **Criteria E: Me and Miscellaneous.** The setting never applies to me or to the "unknown / miscellaneous" bucket.
- [ ] **Criteria F: Settings are remembered.** After a page reload, the newcomer default, hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the Layering switch and the layer order are restored as I left them. The newcomer default is one preference for all rooms; the other settings are saved per room, like #116's directory. This replaces the "resets on reload" criteria of #116, #81 (G) and #82 (F).
- [ ] **Criteria G: Local only.** Saved settings stay on this device. They are never synced to other collaborators, included in exported files or shared links, or added to undo/redo history.
- [ ] **Criteria H: Shared-state integrity.** Applying the default or restoring saved settings changes no element (`index` and `version` stay the same) and sends nothing new to other collaborators.
- [ ] **Criteria I: Safe restore.** Saved settings that refer to collaborators no longer known, or that are unreadable or from an older version, are ignored without errors, falling back to the defaults. Hiding my own drawings is not restored on reload, so a room never opens stuck in view mode (#116 forces view mode while my own drawings are hidden).

## Resolved Questions

- **Who is "new"?** Anyone this client sees for the first time, meaning they aren't in #116's collaborator directory yet.
- **Does changing the default affect people already here?** No, only future newcomers (Criteria C).
- **Where do newcomers go in the layer order?** Below everyone already in it: directly above Miscellaneous, or at the very bottom if I've moved Miscellaneous up (Criteria D, amended in the comment below).
- **Can the default control what the newcomer sees?** No. Like the rest of #14, it only changes what *I* see on my own screen.

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Controlling what other collaborators see, or any server-side permissions.
- Syncing settings between devices or accounts.
- Notifying me when a newcomer joins.
- Per-room newcomer defaults.
- Changes to how ownership, co-ownership (#84) or the layer ordering rule itself work.

## Related

- **Depends on:** #116 (directory, visibility), #81 (locking), #82 (layer order; PR #180, which this issue changes in Criteria D)
- **Design decisions:** see the Design comment below

## Head Issue

Issue (#14): Allow a togglable Layer in which all users are compartmentalized by interactivity and visibility. (#14: "A default for new joining users so that you don't have to see all users.")
